title: Traffic session coordinator SDK + endpoints for consistent canary/shadow exposure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: client SDKs and multi-step request flows cause inconsistent exposure during canary/A-B/shadow experiments (retries, batching, sticky sessions across devices). We need a lightweight session coordination primitive in the control plane and complementary SDK helpers so that a single logical user/session consistently routes to the same rollout variant for the duration of an experiment and so telemetry is attributable. This ticket implements the server-side 'rollout session' API, client lifecycle helpers, and permission scopes for session creation/inspection. Will also add idempotency semantics for session creation and rollback-safe session revocation.
acceptance_criteria: Create session endpoint accepts client-provided idempotency token and returns a session id with variant assignment
SDK exposes helpers to create/attach/refresh session with automatic retry and exponential backoff
Session assignment is sticky across retries, batching, and KV-cache-backed inference requests for N minutes (configurable)
Audit logs record session create/extend/revoke with actor and rollout id
Traffic simulation harness shows <1% drift between expected and observed variant exposure over 1M simulated requests
Permissions enforced: rollout:session:create and rollout:session:inspect scopes required; lack of permission returns 403
design_decisions: Server-side session object (control plane) chosen over pure client-signed tokens to centralize audit, allow revocation and easy metrics aggregation
Idempotency: clients supply Idempotency-Key header at creation; server stores short-lived idempotency record keyed by (client-id, idempotency-key, rollout-id)
Session TTL default 30 minutes; SDK auto-refresh API available to extend by explicit call; server supports PATCH to extend TTL
Session binding resolution occurs during routing stage so that batched requests preserve variant assignment via session id / session cookie
We will not encrypt session payloads client-side; session ids are opaque GUIDs and have short TTLs and RBAC controls for inspection
api_contract: POST /v1/rollout-sessions  - request: { rollout_id, client_context?, idempotency_key? } - response: { session_id, variant, ttl, assigned_at }
GET /v1/rollout-sessions/{session_id} - returns session metadata and assigned variant (permission: rollout:session:inspect)
PATCH /v1/rollout-sessions/{session_id} - body: { extend_ttl_minutes } - extends session if owner or admin
DELETE /v1/rollout-sessions/{session_id} - revokes session (used during rollback); revocation triggers immediate routing fallback
sdk_helpers: SessionManager.createOrGet(rolloutId, opts) - handles idempotency token generation and retry semantics
SessionManager.attachToRequest(req) - injects session_id header and local sticky cache to survive batching
SessionManager.refresh(sessionId) - safe refresh helper that re-auths and extends TTL
Mobile/Web: automatic persistence with secure storage and cross-device strategy guidance in SDK docs
Telemetry helpers: SDK emits rollout.session.created, .refreshed, .revoked events to telemetry endpoint for counting and attribution
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store lifecycle (create, dedupe, expiry)
Integration tests: end-to-end flow with SDK + gateway ensuring sticky assignment across retry and batching scenarios
Chaos test: simulate gateway failover and ensure session revocation triggers fallback to default model variant without user-visible errors
Load test: 100k concurrent session creations across 10 rollouts, measure DB write amplification and latency
E2E canary: enable behind internal feature flag, test on internal beta tenants (10% of internal traffic) before external canary
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): feature flag on dev cluster, SDK integration tests, pass internal telemetry checks
Phase 1 (beta): enable for internal customers and Redwood playgrounds, 5% traffic, monitor exposure drift and error rates for 48h
Phase 2 (canary): 10% external production traffic, enable automatic rollback if error rate > 0.5% or exposure drift > 2%
Phase 3 (GA): documentation, public SDK release, migration guide, opt-in for existing rollout APIs
Rollback policy: immediate revoke of sessions for affected rollout_id and global fallback to stable variant; automatic revert if metric thresholds exceeded
notes: Priority is high because inconsistent exposure has caused two customer-facing regressions in the last quarter
Design reviewed by Marta Alvarez (APAC infra lead) on 2026-03-09; main feedback was to ensure minimal token size and clear audit trail
Performance concern: short-lived idempotency store will increase write QPS; plan to shard by rollout_id and TTL-evict via background sweeper
Follow-up: Add RBAC matrix mapping token scopes to rollout operations and surface in Console (PM ticket to own)
PR for runtime integration (gateway routing + session lookup) will be separate: ENG-20412
